guidance: Approve provision-specific applicability and transition analysis; use readiness labels before applicable dates. Explorer/consolidation aids research; authentic Official Journal acts govern. Art.10(5) has been deleted; current sensitive-category bias processing requires assessment of Art.4a and data-protection law. From 2 December 2026, screen Art 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb) (non-consensual intimate imagery of an identifiable person; child sexual abuse material) under the provider and deployer conditions of Art 5(1a) and Art 5(1b). Art 4a(1) covers providers of high-risk systems under six cumulative conditions; Art 4a(2) extends the same safeguards to other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and creates no obligation to carry out bias detection. Art 50: the Commission guidelines C(2026) 7702 final are non-binding; the Code of Practice of 10 Jun 2026 is assessed adequate for Art 50(2), (4) and (5), but adherence is not conclusive evidence of compliance and gives no presumption of conformity. Entries flagged for legal review are pending qualified legal review and must not be presented as settled law.

Requirement-level applicability rows are not yet derived from them.

obligations.scope: Selective audit prompts for Articles 9-15, Annex IV, Article 50 and associated actor duties; grouped references are explicit and this is not an exhaustive EU AI Act catalog.

applicationContext.legalSource: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(i) and (ii), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Art 1, point (40)(b)
applicationContext.covers: Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 except Article 6(5)
applicationContext.approvalRule: Dates inform review; they do not automatically approve applicability. Assess Articles 2 and 111, route, actor, intended use, relevant modifications and sectoral rules. Article 111(2), as replaced: for high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III date of their route (2 December 2027 for Annex III, 2 August 2028 for Annex I), the Regulation applies only if their design changes significantly from that date, and the first unit of the type and model sets the date (recital (39) of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744); the cut-off is no longer the fixed 2 August 2026. Legacy systems intended for use by public authorities comply by 2 August 2030 whatever their design changes; components of the Annex X large-scale IT systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 sit outside Article 111(2) and comply by 31 December 2030 (Article 111(1)). Article 5 applies to legacy systems. Annex I Section B requires sectoral-route analysis under Article 2(2), rather than automatic direct Section 2 application. These rules are pending legal review (LR-03, LR-10).
applicationContext.sourceCurrencyRule: Source publication, research and application dates have different meanings. A new source version creates an impact-review candidate and never rewrites a historical decision.

decisionPolicy.providerResponsibility: Articles 9-15 are system requirements; provider responsibility is linked through Article 16(a). A deployer may inspect provider evidence but does not thereby assume every provider duty. Article 25 role changes need separate review.
decisionPolicy.dataScope: Under Article 10(1), datasets used for data-trained models are assessed; Article 10(6) limits Article 10(2)-(4) and Article 4a(1) to testing datasets for systems without model training. Article 10(5) was deleted; special-category processing is a separate Article 4a/data-protection assessment, not an upload permission. Article 4a(2) extends the same conditions and safeguards to providers and deployers of other AI systems and models and to deployers of high-risk systems, and creates no obligation to carry out bias detection and correction.
decisionPolicy.retention: Retention is actor, control, purpose and law dependent. Article 26(6) is not one universal evidence-vault retention policy.
decisionPolicy.excludedActorDuties: Other provider, deployer, representative, importer, distributor, sectoral, conformity, registration and fundamental-rights duties must be added where applicable. This selective catalog does not waive them.

factDerivations.rule: A derived fact is true if any listed fact is true, false if all are false, otherwise unknown (docs/research/art50-transparency-2026-11.json, vocabularies.derivationRule). Classification never asks a derived fact directly. For art50DisclosureApplies, the facts of a role the operator does not hold (provider: interactsDirectlyWithNaturalPersons, generatesSyntheticContent; deployer: the other three) count as false.

obligations.dateFacts: The rule pack's application-date predicates (templates/catalog.json, regulatorySnapshot.applicationDates) use eight facts: generatesSyntheticContent, placedOnMarketDate, highRiskRoute, firstPlacedOnMarketOrPutIntoServiceDate, significantDesignChangeOnOrAfterChapterIIIDate, intendedForUseByPublicAuthorities, annexXLargeScaleItComponent and gpaiModelPlacedOnMarketDate. The guided classification records each of them as true, false or unknown (dates as YYYY-MM-DD or unknown): highRiskRoute from the reviewed route and the Article 6(3) derogation, generatesSyntheticContent from the four modality facts. A predicate that reads an unknown fact yields needs_information.

exclusionType.exclusions: A triggered item is excluded when the ifAll list of any of its exclusions is true; if none is true and one is unknown, the item needs information. An exclusion takes effect only with fact values the independent classification review approved; exclusions with basis 'guidance' rest on non-binding guidelines and stay pending legal review.
exclusionType.exceptionsTestedPerItem: Decision of 6 November 2026 (option a): a statutory exception claimed under Article 50(1), (3) or (4) never excludes the item. It is tested per output, channel or deployment in fieldwork (the model is criterion A50-P-04B-C01: label present or exception supported), so the item stays a candidate.
exclusionType.followsItems: Article 50(5) governs only how the information owed under Article 50(1) to (4) is given, and the scope exclusions of Article 2(6) and 2(10) take the system out of the Regulation. An item with followsItems is evaluated only after its own trigger: it is a candidate when at least one listed item of a role the operator holds is a candidate; otherwise it needs information when one of them needs information; otherwise it is excluded when one of them is excluded (with that item's exclusion); otherwise it is not triggered.

triggerType.evaluation: Candidate selection only. Unknown in a required predicate yields needs_information. Legal-period approval and scope exclusions are separate human decisions.
